title: Show the default gateway (router address) of this Mac
summary: The default gateway is the router address your Mac sends internet traffic to. Showing it in Terminal helps find out whether the problem is in your Mac, the router, or the internet provider.

aliases.text: what is my router ip on mac
no internet mac check router ip
какой ip у роутера на макбуке

steps.explain: Show the default route. The line 'gateway:' is the router address the Mac uses for internet traffic; 'interface:' is the network connection it uses (for example en0 for Wi-Fi). This command only reads the routing table and changes nothing.
steps.expect: Lines such as 'gateway: 192.168.1.1' and 'interface: en0'. If no 'gateway:' line appears, the Mac has no default route, which usually means it is not connected to a network.

alternatives.explain: Show the whole IPv4 routing table. Look for the line that starts with 'default'; the second column is the gateway address.

steps.explain: Send three test packets to the router to check that it answers. Replace <GATEWAY_IP> with the gateway address from the previous step. Press Ctrl+C to stop early.

placeholders.name: GATEWAY_IP
placeholders.description: The router address shown as 'gateway:' in the previous step.

steps.expect: Ends with '3 packets transmitted, 3 packets received, 0.0% packet loss'. If packets are lost or there is no answer, the problem is between your Mac and the router (Wi-Fi or cable).

verify.expect: A 'gateway:' line with an IP address. If it is missing, the Mac has no default route.

warnings: The gateway address is usually a private address like 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x. Do not share it publicly.
